title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 27-31 of the notes). A stratified space is encoded as a topological category Σ: objects Σ(0), arrows Σ(1), identity section δ, and a 'bord' map b : Σ(1) → Σ(0) (source or target). The previous page imposes three conditions. (a) b is a proper immersion, so δ(Σ(0)) is open and closed and Σ(1) ≅ δ(Σ(0)) ⊔ Σ*(1), where Σ*(1) is the set of non-identity arrows. (b) b restricted to Σ*(1) is an immersion with rare (nowhere dense) image. (c) Connected components of Σ(0) are finite-dimensional. A dimension count then gives Σ*_ii = ∅: the only arrows inside a connected component are identities. So the canonical functor Σ → I, with I = π0(Σ) preordered by existence of arrows, contracts each component.

This page adds (d): every invertible arrow is an identity, i.e. Σ is (the category of) a topological ordered set. One then concludes 'aisément' two things. First, I is a genuine order (antisymmetric). Second, a non-identity arrow u ∈ Σ*(1) has non-identity image in I. So when Σ comes from an ordered topological space Σ = Σ(0), the projection Σ → I is strictly increasing.

Grothendieck then returns to an ordered topological space Σ with order relation Σ(1) ⊂ Σ×Σ, decomposed as diagonal ⊔ Σ*(1). It satisfies conditions a), b), c), 1°) of p.27, which correspond to the 'déploiement' (unfolding) of a locally equisingular stratification. It also has finitely many connected components. Take I = π0(Σ) and write Σ_i for the component i and Σ_ij for the arrows from Σ_i to Σ_j. Assume further that for i < j the map Σ_ij → Σ_j is a monomorphism, i.e. a closed embedding. Then the data (Σ_i, Σ_ij, s_ij, t_ij : Σ_ij ⇉ Σ_i, Σ_j) satisfy the axioms a), c), d) of p.28; p.28 axiomatises a déploiement indexed by I.

The next page checks the remaining axiom b): Σ_ik ∩ Σ_jk = ∅ for incomparable i, j < k. This follows because each down-set Σ_{<x} is totally ordered. It then states the conclusion: déploiements of equisingular stratifications indexed by I are equivalent to ordered topological spaces Σ satisfying these conditions, together with a strictly increasing map π0(Σ) → I.

Purpose: a combinatorial-topological model of the 'unfolded' stratified space. The strata are separated and glued only through the boundary/link data Σ_ij, and this is repackaged as a single ordered topological space. It is a step toward the equivalence 'stratified spaces with conical neighbourhoods ⇔ déploiements' announced in the title.
errors: The argument that I is ordered and Σ → I strictly increasing is called 'aisé' but relies on the previous page's dimension argument, which needs Σ*_ii → Σ_i to be a fibration with fibres of non-negative dimension. That is only sketched there.
Finiteness of π0(Σ) and the mono hypothesis on Σ_ij → Σ_j are imposed ad hoc; nothing here says whether they follow from the stratification setting.
No genuine mathematical error is visible; the page is a sketch.

ideas.what: Encoding a stratified space (its unfolding) as a topological category / topological poset, with no non-identity arrows inside a stratum, via a dimension argument
ideas.modern_name: stratified spaces as topological posets / exit-path type categories; unzipping of conically smooth stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lurie (Higher Algebra, App. A, 2010s); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017); Treumann, MacPherson (exit paths)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) §5 sketches a programme of 'tame' stratified spaces and tubular neighbourhoods; details not published

ideas.what: Under 'no non-trivial isomorphisms', π0 of the topological poset is a poset and the projection to it is strictly increasing
ideas.modern_name: stratification map X → P to the poset of strata

ideas.what: Equivalence between 'déploiements' indexed by I (strata Σ_i, boundary pieces Σ_ij with maps to Σ_i, Σ_j, closed embeddings into Σ_j) and ordered topological spaces with a strictly increasing map π0(Σ) → I
ideas.modern_name: resolution of a Thom–Mather stratified space into manifolds with corners carrying iterated fibration structures; AFT unzipping
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thom, Mather (control data); Verona; Albin–Leichtnam–Mazzeo–Piazza (2012); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions the theme only programmatically

missed.claim: Grothendieck repackages the unfolding (déploiement) of a locally equisingular stratification as a single ordered topological space whose components are the unfolded strata. The order arrows Σ_ij encode the boundary/link fibrations. This anticipates the later 'stratified space = space over a poset, with unzipping into manifolds with corners' viewpoint (Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Albin–Mazzeo et al.). The specific axioms (proper immersion of the bord map, rare images, dimension argument forcing a poset) form an independent axiomatisation that does not seem to appear in the literature.
missed.quote: Revenons alors à un ens. ordonné topologique Σ = (Σ(0), Σ(1)=δ(Σ(0))⊔Σ*(1)) ... (correspondant au déploiement d'une stratification localement équisingulière)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It offers a purely order-theoretic-topological characterisation of unfolded stratified spaces. This could be compared with AFT's unzipping and with the 'iterated fibration structure' characterisations, and might give an alternative foundation for tame topology of stratified spaces as envisaged in the Esquisse.

missed.claim: The page imposes finiteness of π0 and closed embedding of Σ_ij → Σ_j as extra hypotheses. Whether these are automatic for déploiements of equisingular stratifications is left open.
missed.quote: et supposons de plus que pour i<j (i,j∈I) Σ_ij → Σ_j soit mono i.e. plongement fermé
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Settling this would make the claimed equivalence 'déploiements ⇔ ordered topological spaces over I' unconditional.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine step in a sketched equivalence, but it belongs to an unpublished axiomatic theory of déploiements of stratified spaces via topological posets. That theory anticipates later work by Lurie, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka and the Mazzeo school, and is only alluded to in the Esquisse. The individual deductions here are elementary.
transcription_corrections: 'Alors on conclut aisément que $\underline{E}$[?] un pré-ordonné $\underline{I}$ est ordonné' should read 'Alors on conclut aisément que le pré-ordonné I est ordonné'.
'et que toute flèche de Σ' reads in the image like 'et que toute flèche'; the sense is unchanged.
'Si Σ est associée à une {+catégorie top.+} ordonnée' appears to read 'Si Σ est associé à un ens. ordonné (un top.), Σ=Σ(0)'.
'{+une strat.+} strictement croissante' probably reads 'est strictement croissante'.
'Σ(1)⊂Σ̂×Σ' likely means the order relation viewed as a subspace of Σ×Σ; the hat is a superscript mark, not a separate space.
The inserted word replacing the struck 'factorisation' is uncertain, possibly 'projection'; 'simplicité' is unlikely.
'mono i.e. plongement {+fermé+}': 'fermé' is written above the line and 'plongement' is underlined.
The folio number is probably 30, given that the next page is numbered 31 and the text refers to pp. 27-28.
